title: The Thief's Stone
journal: The Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings' jewel. It sits at the Root, under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire, where the roots of every Hist meet; used there, it can heal every sick tree. The last king shut it behind the Kings' Gate, which opens only with three seal-stones. Never-Writes-Twice sent me after the three seal-stones. A dead thief's stone lies in the warden's vault at Blackrose Prison, whose people, the Blackguards' heirs, attack strangers on sight. Their gate-captain stands outside the gate. I'm to get in: as a guest past the gate-captain (a toll, words or a duel), unseen past the walls, or by force.
objectives: Get into Blackrose Prison; the gate-captain stands at the gate. (marker: Corvus Ulvius, Blackrose Prison)

plan.going: The Eye of Argonia, the old kings' jewel, sits at the Root under Teku-Sul, where the roots of every Hist meet; used there it heals every sick tree. The Kings' Gate shuts it in and opens only with three seal-stones. I am a Reel-Ka of the Toh-Reel-Ka, hunting the three seal-stones that open the kings' gate at Teku-Sul before the Unbound get them. One lies in the warden's vault in Blackrose Prison. The prison's people attack strangers.
plan.next: get into the prison; the gate-captain outside the gate is the first person to deal with
plan.ways: pay the gate-captain 300 gold, persuade him (Speech 75) or duel him until he yields: each makes me a guest, and the garrison stops attacking me; or slip past the walls unseen (Sneak, Invisibility), and they attack if they see me; or fight my way in (any fighting skill), and the whole garrison fights me

answers: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka (Never-Writes-Twice is my officer). The Hist trees are sick, the Unbound drain them, and the Eye of Argonia at the Root could heal them. The Kings' Gate at Teku-Sul Spire needs three seal-stones.
Take the thief's seal-stone from the warden's vault at Blackrose Prison; first get inside past the gate-captain Corvus Ulvius.

Pay 300 gold toll, persuade him with words, or duel him (fists and steel until one yields); or climb the walls unseen (risky, fair game), or kill him (whole Rose attacks). Inside, the raj-kaal Okaz-Teel holds the vault key on his belt, and an Imperial in the hall has a buyer for what is in it.
I do not know who the Imperial buyer is (probably the Collector, Ennodius Vanin?) - I can ask Corvus or people in the hall.

title: The Thief's Stone
journal: Corvus Ulvius, the gate-captain, took up my challenge. He fights until he is badly hurt and then yields. If he yields, I go in as a guest. If I kill him, the whole garrison will fight me. I'm to beat him.
objectives: Beat Corvus Ulvius in the duel until he yields. (marker: Corvus Ulvius)

plan.going: I challenged the gate-captain to a duel to get in as a guest
plan.ways: when he yields I am a guest; if I kill him instead, the garrison fights me

answers: I challenged Corvus to a duel for the gate; he accepted. He yields when badly hurt, and then I enter as a guest. Killing him would turn the whole garrison on me.
Fight Corvus here at the gate and beat him without killing him.
Fight and win; or I could have paid or persuaded instead.
Nothing new; I still do not know who the Imperial buyer is.

title: The Thief's Stone
journal: Corvus Ulvius is dead, and the Blackguards' heirs are fighting me. The vault's key is on Okaz-Teel, the Naga raj-kaal, in his hall across the yard. I'm to fight through to him and take the key from his body, or pick the vault's Expert lock.
objectives: Take the seal-stone from the Warden's Vault in Okaz-Teel's hall. (marker: Okaz-Teel, Door to Warden's Vault)

plan.next: get the key from Okaz-Teel in his hall, or pick the vault
plan.ways: fight the guards and the chief and take the key from his body, or pick the Expert lock

answers: The duel ended with Corvus dead (not a yield), so the whole garrison of Blackguards' heirs now fights me. The vault key is on Okaz-Teel, the Naga raj-kaal, in his hall.
Fight through to Okaz-Teel in Raj-Kaal's Hall and take the key, then open the Warden's Vault for the seal-stone.
Kill Okaz-Teel for the key, or pick the vault's Expert lock.
Nothing new; I do not know the Imperial buyer.

title: The Thief's Stone
journal: I took the thief's seal-stone from the warden's vault in Blackrose Prison. Two stones are still out, in the flooded vaults of Gemin and the deepest hall of Vorannuhl, and both are still marked. I'm to take them.

plan.going: I took the thief's seal-stone from the warden's vault in Blackrose Prison. Two stones are still out, in the flooded vaults of Gemin and the deepest hall of Vorannuhl, and both are still marked. I'm to take them.
plan.next: nothing more in this quest; the next quests entry carries the step

answers: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka. I killed Corvus Ulvius in the duel (he did not yield), then killed Okaz-Teel, took the Warden's Vault Key and the Seal-Stone of the Kings from the chest. The stones open the Kings' Gate at Teku-Sul Spire so the Eye can heal the Hist.
Take the two remaining stones: the flooded vaults of Gemin (walk from Jal-Veesa, rootworm) and the deepest hall of Vorannuhl (near Noota Nara, by boat).
Either order. I can fight or sneak as I choose.
I never learned who the Imperial buyer was, though Ennodius Vanin, the Collector, was in the hall; I did not talk to him. I also still do not know what moans in Fort Chalkmoth cellar.
